record.context_brief: Asymptotic enumeration of labeled C4-free graphs.
record.original_question: Let C4 denote the 4-cycle, and let f(n; C4) be the number of labeled graphs on n vertices that do not contain C4 as a subgraph. Is it true that f(n; C4) = 2^((1/2 + o(1)) n^(3/2)) as n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: As far as I know f(n; C4) = 2^(1/2 + o(1))n3/2 is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C_4$ denote the cycle on four vertices. For a positive integer $n$, let $f(n;C_4)$ denote the number of labeled simple graphs on the vertex set $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ that contain no copy of $C_4$ as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph. Determine whether
$$f(n;C_4) = 2^{\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1)\right) n^{3/2}}\qquad\text{as } n\to\infty.$$
Equivalently, is it true that $\log_2 f(n;C_4) \sim \tfrac{1}{2} n^{3/2}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The lower bound $f(n;C_4)\ge 2^{\mathrm{ex}(n,C_4)}=2^{(1/2+o(1))n^{3/2}}$ is immediate from extremal $C_4$-free graphs, and Kleitman–Winston proved an upper bound of the form $2^{c\,n^{3/2}}$ for some constant $c$, but the matching constant $c=1/2$ remains unproven. Surveys on enumeration of $H$-free graphs for bipartite $H$ continue to list this as open: even the correct constant in the exponent for $C_4$-free graphs is not known.

status_evidence.title: On the number of graphs without 4-cycles (Kleitman–Winston)
status_evidence.snippet: Kleitman and Winston proved f_n(C_4) ≤ 2^{c n^{3/2}}.
status_evidence.claim: The known upper bound is 2^{c n^{3/2}} with some constant c, not necessarily 1/2.

status_evidence.title: The number of K_{m,m}-free graphs (Combinatorica)
status_evidence.snippet: For most bipartite H, even the correct order of magnitude of log_2 f_n(H) is not known; the conjecture f_n(H) = 2^{(1+o(1)) ex(n,H)} is open.
status_evidence.claim: For bipartite forbidden subgraphs including C_4, sharp enumeration constants remain open.

status_evidence.title: Almost All C_4-Free Graphs Have Fewer than (1−ε) ex(n,C_4) Edges
status_evidence.snippet: Structural result about typical C_4-free graphs, but does not resolve the leading constant in log_2 f(n;C_4).
status_evidence.claim: Recent structural work on C_4-free graphs does not establish the conjectured constant 1/2.
